r3_clip_region — 2D region op

• Data kinds: region → region

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "r3_clip_region", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

• HALCON equivalent: clip_region (the HALCON reference is a useful guide to its meaning and parameters)

Usage

Clips the region with a rectangular window centred on the image (equivalent to HALCON clip_region).

a is the fraction of height to keep (0 to 1), b the fraction of width to keep (0 to 1). The window is placed at the image centre, and all region pixels outside the window are erased.

The window size is wh = max(1, round(a*H)) rows × ww = max(1, round(b*W)) columns, with its top-left at ((H-wh)//2, (W-ww)//2) (remainders lean to top/left). a, b are clipped to [0,1], 0.5 if non-finite. a=b=1 returns the input unchanged; even a=b=0 keeps the 1 central pixel (it never becomes all zero). The input is turned into a foreground mask with > 0.5, so grey values and NaN are treated as background.

Returns a float64 0/1 mask of the same shape as the input. Note that the window is based on the whole image, not on the region's bounding rectangle (if the region is in a corner of the image, a=b=0.5 may erase it entirely). For a relative clip based on the region, use hx_clip_region_rel. It erases outside the window; it does not make the window itself foreground (where there is no region it stays 0). Cutting the same central window on the image side is it_crop_domain (which uses 1 a for the same fraction vertically and horizontally); keeping contour points with a window is xg_crop_contours. On exception it falls back to a 0 mask, recorded in the backend_safe ledger (re-raised in strict mode).
